title: Checkpoint 5 — Putting It All Together
description: Quick check after Build #4: sensor readings drive the LED color.

questions.prompt: In the default humidity mode, what color shows when humidity is below 30% (very dry)?
questions.explanation: Below 30% → Red (very dry). The ranges climb: yellow, green, then blue as it gets more humid.

questions.prompt: Humidity reads 60% — comfortable. What color does the LED show?
It's really humid — above 70%. What color appears?
questions.explanation: Above 70% → Blue (very humid). 30–50% would be yellow.

questions.prompt: Why is humidity (not temperature) the default thing we react to?
choices: Breathing on the sensor changes humidity instantly, so you see the effect right away
Temperature can't be measured by the DHT22
Humidity is the only thing the ESP32 understands
The RGB LED only reacts to humidity
questions.explanation: Instant feedback makes cause-and-effect obvious — temperature changes too slowly to demo.

questions.prompt: What is the if / else-if structure in the loop doing?
choices: Mapping ranges of sensor values to different colors
Printing the code to the screen
questions.explanation: Each if/else-if checks a range and picks the matching color — that's the 'logic' step.
